column5: Flexible polyurethane cushion foam removed from an overstuffed chair. Source metadata describes a 0.75 m by 0.75 m by 0.2 m cushion; the stock-thickness coordinate is the original cushion thickness, not HFM sample thickness. This profile selects the R1 experiments only: heat capacity on 2021-04-05 and conductivity on 2021-02-19. The separately recorded R2 capacity sample is 33.11 mm thick, versus 50.96 mm for R1, so it is not pooled into this selected approximately 51 mm sample profile. Specimen labels and similar thickness do not establish exact coupon continuity, equal compression, or identical porosity across dates. No moisture, contact pressure, isotropy, compression-response, aging, strength, expansion, fire/degradation or service-temperature law is inferred from these thermal experiments.

The Wet label in raw filenames denotes unconditioned samples kept indoors at 22 +/- 3 degC and relative humidity 40 +/- 20 percent. It does not mean water-saturated, nor does it supply exact sample moisture or zero moisture. These specimens are not assigned the source's separate oven-dried condition. The general conductivity method is ASTM C518 with through-thickness upward heat flow; the general capacity method is ASTM C1784-20 with equal-temperature plate steps. Applied contact pressure, calibrated instrument uncertainty, specimen-axis mapping and cross-property covariance are not provided. Conductivity and capacity are distinct runs; joint thermal use is conditional on treating the selected product/conditioning population as representative, not proof of identical coupons or independent measurements.

Instrument thickness 50.96 mm. Raw result mean temperatures 10,20.01,30.01,40.01 degC give 54854,53861,58335,61219 J/(m3 K). The instrument's Specific Heat column carries volume units, not J/(kg K). Equal-plate heating uses 5 to 15, 15 to 25, 25 to 35 and 35 to 45 degC steps. These are finite-step estimates reported at their mean temperatures. No per-run standard uncertainty is supplied.
